title: Jude and the Radiators
premise: August Pemberton has tuned the radiators of the Vane family's decaying mansion for twenty years, listening through the pipes to the arguments, silences, and one unrecorded song the late matriarch, Iris Vane, hummed only to her. When a radio station plays that song—credited to Iris's estranged son Theo—August realizes someone in the house sold a memory she thought was hers alone. As Iris's dementia deepens and the family gathers to contest the will, August must decide whether to remain the invisible witness or reveal what she knows: that the song was written for her, and that Iris's final wish was never about the house at all. The novel ends with August claiming her place at the piano in the emptied parlor, playing the song back into the radiators as the new owner—a found-family collective of the household staff—hears it for the first time.
about_author: Sebastian Almeida is a former building superintendent who spent a decade listening to the mechanical heartbeats of old houses before turning to fiction. His stories have appeared in small literary journals, and this is his first novel.

chapters.title: The Inventory of Unsaid Things
chapters.summary: August's POV. She makes her autumn tuning visit to Vane House, cataloguing radiators like rooms of memory: the nursery pipe that whistles Iris's lullaby, the parlor radiator gone cold since the funeral. We learn she kept every secret the pipes ever carried her. Emotional beat: tender routine masking loneliness.

chapters.title: A Song on the Airwaves
chapters.summary: August's POV. Driving home, a late-night radio program plays the lullaby—arranged, recorded, credited to Theo Vane. August pulls over, shaking; the song existed only between her and Iris. Beat: violation and vertigo, the invisible woman made suddenly central to something she never chose.

chapters.title: Theo Comes Home
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with Theo, who returns to prepare the estate sale, carrying guilt he won't name. He is charming, evasive, and startled to find August still employed by a dead woman's trust. Beat: two keepers of secrets circling each other, each convinced the other is the thief.

chapters.title: What the Pipes Remember
chapters.summary: August's POV. She traces the recording's provenance through the house itself: a portable recorder in the music room, a sister's old bedroom, dates scratched inside radiator panels. Flashbacks layer Iris teaching her the song over three winters. Beat: grief braided with detective resolve.

chapters.title: The Gathering
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV shifts. The four Vane siblings arrive for the reading of the will, each performing a version of devotion while quietly looting drawers. August serves tea and listens to the radiators carry their whispers upstairs. Beat: satirical tension, power assembling itself around a dying memory.

chapters.title: Iris, Mostly
chapters.summary: August's POV. She visits Iris in the care facility; lucid moments surface like bubbles. Iris grips her wrist: 'You know which one of them took it. Say it before I can't.' August promises nothing. Beat: the weight of being trusted by someone losing the ability to verify anything.

chapters.title: The Reading
chapters.summary: Lawyer's office, rotating sibling POVs. The will leaves the house not to any child but 'to whoever can play the song'—a riddle they assume refers to sheet music hidden somewhere. Suspicion detonates among them. Beat: inheritance as weapon, family arranged around a question no one will ask aloud.

chapters.title: Confession in a Cold Room
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Cornered by August in the shut-down parlor, he admits he recorded Iris secretly years ago and sold the arrangement to pay debts—but insists he never knew what the song meant to his mother. August tells him whom it was written for. Beat: shame meeting truth; neither leaves clean.

chapters.title: The Question
chapters.summary: August's POV, climax. At the estate auction she stands before the whole family and asks the question the house arranged itself around: who did Iris love enough to write for? She plays the lullaby from memory on the parlor piano. Iris, brought to the window by a nurse, mouths the words. Beat: exposure as liberation.

chapters.title: Steam Rising
chapters.summary: August's POV, resolution. The staff pool their savings and buy the house; the siblings take money and leave. On the first cold night, August bleeds the radiators herself, and steam carries the song through every room as the new household—cook, gardener, nurse, Theo forgiven but not absolved—listens. Beat: quiet triumph, found family, warmth made literal.
